title: Far addressing folds other than the runtime-index fold leave dangling DBG_VALUEs
summary: Three far addressing-mode folds erase or rewrite an access and leave the G_PTR_ADDs that computed its pointer with only debug uses: the absolute-long fold (tryFarAbsoluteAddressing, #320-2), the [dp],Y displacement window in tryFarIndirectIndexedAddressing (#320-4), and the absolute-long indexed fold (tryFarAbsoluteIndexedAddressing, far-word patch 5 / downstream 0061). The legalizer erases the dead adds; salvageDebugInfoForDbgValue cannot express a G_PTR_ADD and leaves the DBG_VALUE on the erased register, which DetectDeadLanes marks undef, so -g with -verify-machineinstrs fails ("Generic virtual register use cannot be undef"). The simplest -g far field access (base + 1) fails at O0 and O2 on the reviewed split and on the downstream release toolchain. Emitted code is unaffected. This is the mechanism of mos-far-index-fold-dangling-dbg (B4) at the fold sites its repair did not cover.

unknowns: Downstream 0002 is not repaired: vendor/ and 0002 were held by another agent on 2026-10-01. The repair (dropDeadFarAddressDebugUses, called by every far fold) exists only in the #320 split series, branch split-320-321-r2 and pkt-r2-far-word, and is recorded below as additional runs; the status stays confirmed until the downstream toolchain carries it.
Release builds without -verify-machineinstrs were not examined for the resulting location; for B4 the location degraded to $noreg without the verifier.

prior_work.source_assessment: The reviewed split (#320-2, #320-4, far-word patch 5) and downstream 0002/0061 drop dead-address debug locations only in tryFarRuntimeIndexFold (the B4 repair). The absolute-long, displacement-window and absolute-indexed folds erase or rewrite the access without touching the debug users of the adds that become dead.
prior_work.binary_assessment: Reviewed split llc c-320-04 and far-word candidate c-fw-14 (assertions) exit 134 with the signature for field.ll, store1.ll and gfield.ll (O0), and c-fw-14 for gidx.ll; the downstream release candidate llc f1fa50a2 fails field.ll and gidx.ll the same way.
prior_work.decision: mos-far-index-fold-dangling-dbg is correctly closed for its own site: its same-input regression passes and its causal change covers only tryFarRuntimeIndexFold. These inputs pass on #320-3 and fail through different fold functions whose code the B4 repair never touched, so they are a distinct defect instance with their own baseline rather than a reopening of B4.
